section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Above all a eulogy: every speaker laments his loss, tells how they bonded with him and what they loved about him, and celebrates him. The brief asks for nine people on their feet in one room, each saying what there is to say about the dead man: a eulogy, not a two-voice dialogue. Spine is mixed: Thomas is an original character and not in the corpus, so no event or scene names him; sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in (the Pragia aftermath, the run-up to Omega-4, Tuchanka, Rannoch, the Citadel shore leave, Grissom, the final push) and the speaker's own record of those. Jack holds the first and last turns (~2,500 words each, long as asked), the other seven run 450-1,000 (Grunt, EDI, James short and blunt; Liara, Joker, Tali fullest). Nine sections is inside the form's 6-14 range. Each turn opens by picking up the one before: Jack's grief to Tali's engine room, Tali's hospital-and-hands to Joker's bad days, Joker's jokes to Liara's late nights, Liara's mother story to Grunt's blunt question, Grunt's kitchen guarding to James's training and banter, James's Hammer glimpse to Wrex, Wrex's speech to EDI's data, EDI's four-leaf-clover tally back to Jack. Alcohol and music run through the turns as the room's furniture (Thomas's disco, pop, rock, rap, metal, folk, gabber, electro, and black-metal playlists, ryncol, the taped-up recipes), not as a section of their own. Canon branch: genophage cured, Wrex leads the krogan, geth-quarian peace (Legion dead), Grunt alive, Thane dead; crew do not know what Shepard chose, and his death is unconfirmed. Thomas's unfinished poems for Jack are private to Jack; the French lines are his to be quoted sparingly and, per memory rules, never verbatim-perfect by anyone but Jack.

required_facts.fact: Tali'Zorah vas Neema, a young quarian woman who was one of Commander Shepard's most loyal companions during the fight against Saren, has earned her adult name through service and has been integrated into the Migrant Fleet as a full citizen. The Admiralty Board of the quarian fleet assigns her to a classified research mission to investigate anomalous activity in the star of Haestrom, a quarian colony world long abandoned to the geth after their extinction event. The primary objective is to study the planet's rapidly dying sun to understand its unusual behavior. Tali's strike team, including experienced marine commander Kal'Reegar, is deployed to Haestrom to conduct on-site observations. However, the team encounters unexpectedly fierce geth resistance, including multiple troop types (Troopers, Rocket Troopers, Hunters, Destroyers, Recon Drones, Primes, and even a towering Geth Colossus) and extreme solar radiation that strips kinetic and biotic shields, forcing Shepard's squad to navigate between safe shaded areas. When Shepard arrives to investigate Tali's team, they find all of the quarian marines slain except for Kal'Reegar, the sole survivor. Shepard must navigate the research facility while contending with Geth forces and the lethal radiation. The mission culminates at an observatory where Tali has positioned herself with final defensive measures. To advance, Shepard must retrieve two demolition charges from nearby structures to destroy a pillar blocking the path forward. In the final confrontation, the Geth Colossus—equipped with a powerful self-repair ability—presents a formidable obstacle. Shepard has the choice to use a Paragon interrupt to convince Kal'Reegar to stand down from providing covering fire, or to permit him to continue firing at the risk of his own death. Shepard must close to melee range to permanently disable the Colossus' regeneration protocol, destroy the construct, and eliminate waves of geth reinforcements. After the battle, Tali is successfully recruited and evacuated to the Normandy SR-2. If Kal'Reegar survives, he uploads the mission data to the Admiralty Board; if he does not survive, Tali uploads it herself, tormented by the loss of her entire team. Tali integrates into the Normandy's main engineering section alongside Gabriella Daniels and Kenneth Donnelly. Her father, Admiral Rael'Zorah, sends a message confirming her approved transfer and warning that negligence leading to her death will bring severe consequences. The mission's non-completion would prevent Tali from being recruited and would guarantee squad deaths during the suicide mission due to inability to upgrade the Normandy's shields.

In 2186 the quarian Migrant Fleet launched an all-out war to retake Rannoch, catching the geth mid-construction of their megastructure. When the flotilla bombarded and destroyed the structure, killing many programs and dimming the consensus, the surviving geth accepted Reaper code and Reaper upgrades to survive - which turned the war in their favour and pushed the quarians to the brink. Both fleets appealed to Commander Shepard. Shepard first infiltrated a geth dreadnought over Rannoch and freed Legion (or, if Legion was lost, a Geth VI) that had been wired into the drive core as the Reapers' signal booster, shutting the dreadnought down. Shepard then made planetfall and, painting the target for orbital fire, destroyed the Reaper on the surface that was broadcasting the control signal, freeing the geth fleet from Reaper command; dialogue lets Shepard frame this as vengeance for the pre-Prothean species harvested to build that Reaper. With the geth free but the quarians still attacking, Legion sought to upload the Reaper-derived code to grant every geth true individual consciousness, while Tali'Zorah feared it would doom her people. Shepard moderated the standoff (per `geth_quarian` and `rannoch`). Allowing the upload without brokering peace gives the geth full sentience and their fleet to the war but sees the quarian fleet destroyed, with Admiral Koris and Tali possibly lost. Refusing the upload wipes out the geth and leaves the quarians to reclaim Rannoch. A successful reputation check - requiring Legion alive, both Tali and Legion loyal, the heretics rewritten and the Tali/Legion history reconciled - brokers a ceasefire: the geth help the quarians resettle Rannoch, some even uploading into quarian suits to rebuild their immune systems, and both fleets join the war. In every branch the unit (Legion or the Geth VI) sacrifices itself to complete or enable the upload.

A short, conversation-only mission acquired after the failed Cerberus coup on the Citadel. Admiral Hackett told Commander Shepard that the quarian Migrant Fleet was willing to contribute technical specialists and support ships to the Crucible war effort, and directed the Normandy to the Far Rim. Shepard travelled to the Dholen system and docked with a Quarian Envoy Ship. In the Normandy's war room the Admiralty Board of the Migrant Fleet explained that, emboldened after the Reapers gave the geth upgrades, they had abandoned their long isolation and launched an open war to retake the quarian homeworld Rannoch, driving the geth back toward the planet - but the offensive had stalled and their fleet was now exposed. The admirals asked the Normandy to help disable a geth dreadnought that was broadcasting the Reaper control signal and turning the battle against them. If Tali'Zorah had survived the Collector Base she returned to the squad. If she had not been exiled at her father Rael'Zorah's treason trial she now sat on the Admiralty Board in his place; if she had been exiled, the other admirals still brought her in secretly for her knowledge of the geth, which Shepard could needle as their "dirty little secret." Shepard could speak privately with Tali in the captain's cabin to continue or lock in a romance, which on a first playthrough unlocked the Energy Drain bonus power. Afterward Admiral Shala'Raan vas Tonbay took up residence in the war room, Tali joined as a temporary squadmate, and Priority: Geth Dreadnought became available.

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.

beats.text: After the Normandy's bombing run cracked the Reaper base open, a Reaper Destroyer climbed out of the crater. Legion secured a geth ship and flew the squad clear while Shepard manned its turret and called in an orbital strike that briefly downed the Reaper. EDI synced the quarian fleet to the Normandy's targeting systems, and Shepard stayed on the plateau alone, dodging the Destroyer's beam through three targeting solutions and a final slow-motion shot while the fleet fired. Mortally hit, the Reaper addressed Shepard by name, said Harbinger judged the Commander a worthy opponent, spoke of Reapers as "order" against organic "chaos" and the harvest as necessary "intervention," and — if no interrupt was taken — left the threat, "Finish your war. We will be waiting."
With the Reaper down, the geth are weakened and Admiral Han'Gerrel throws the whole quarian fleet at them.

The geth unit rescued from the dreadnought — Legion, or a VI built in its likeness — moves to upload the Reaper code and restore the geth to full strength, which would catch the quarian fleet unready and destroy it.
Stopped from uploading, it turns hostile, and Tali kills it with her boot knife to save Shepard.
Allowed to upload, Tali watches the entire Migrant Fleet come down burning through Rannoch's atmosphere, takes off her mask, says she is sorry, and steps off the cliff before Shepard can reach her.

variants.text: If Legion was sold to Cerberus, never activated, or died at the Collector Base, the unit rescued from the dreadnought is the Geth VI — physically Legion's twin down to the holographic N7 shoulder piece and the hole in its torso, but with no memory of anything after Saren's attack on Eden Prime and a colder view of organics, and it insists throughout "We are not Legion." No peaceful outcome is possible with the VI present. If Shepard lets the geth die, the VI violently assaults Shepard — "[our people] were correct to distrust organics" — and tries to upload the Reaper code before Tali knifes it in the back, or, if Tali is absent, Shala'Raan kills it with a shotgun; the quarians then win the battle overhead. If Shepard uploads the code to save the geth, the VI thanks Shepard, says its "skepticism was misplaced," and dissolves itself into the consensus to grant every geth true intelligence, and the upgraded geth defeat the quarian fleet.

beats.text: Tali proposes using the Normandy's weapon sinks to extend stealth mode, borrowing the idea from quarian practice during drive core discharge.
Adams, Donnelly and Daniels all try to talk her out of it — the SR-2 is state of the art and may not take kindly to being tampered with — and then let her do it anyway, because they trust her.

scenes.when: 2185, across the run-up to the Omega 4 Relay
scenes.where: the engineering deck of the Normandy SR-2

beats.text: They graduated the same class at a tech academy and served together on the SSV Perugia at the Battle of the Citadel. When the Alliance buried the Reapers afterwards, Kenneth defended Shepard loudly enough to border on insubordination — not court-martialled only because he was too good an engineer — and that is what got the Illusive Man's attention.
Gabby made her own inclusion a condition of his Cerberus contract, on the grounds that he would fall apart without her. She also just loves starship engines and was not going to pass up the SR-2.
Neither of them seems to know much about what Cerberus actually does. Kenneth's stated reason for signing on is to kick the Collectors right in the daddy-bags.

Their standing maintenance headache is the FBA arrays. Kenneth starts on the full technical description; Gabby cuts him off and tells Shepard they need FBA couplings. Buy them and Kenneth invites the Commander to a game of Skyllian-five poker, which Shepard can join, decline, or forbid outright.

Kenneth comments on the women aboard — Tali's suit fitting in all the right places, Jack being simultaneously attractive and vicious, Miranda's uniform — and Gabby scolds him every time. After Jack comes aboard she teases him about the new crew member who wears nothing but tattoos from the waist up, waits until he means to go introduce himself, and then mentions the murders.
Both of them are taken when the Collectors board the Normandy, and both die if the rescue comes too late.

evidence.section: *10/30/2010 \- "Reversal" Treatment Allows Dextro/Levo Species to Share Cuisines*
evidence.text: *“The process is quite literally stomach\-turning, but gourmands across the galaxy are lining up to try Reversal, a new gastrointestinal immunosuppressant treatment that allows dextro/levo species to safely sample each other's cuisine. The process is expensive, lasts less than 24 \[Earth Standard] hours, and the food provides no nutrition, but restaurants are already busy booking dextro/levo food parties. "It's an adventure," says food writer and Reversal enthusiast Livian Messalina. "We're opening up new ranges of texture and flavor to each other. Taste still varies from species to species, but that's part of the fun." Doctors are warning these bold new epicures to watch out for leftovers \-\- meals should be eaten as soon as possible, and users must purge before the treatment wears off.”*

evidence.text: Quarians are generally shorter and of slighter build than humans. Quarians have an endoskeleton, lips, teeth, and two eyes with eyelids and tear ducts. Their ears or ear analogues differ in a noticeable fashion from those of humans, with references made to "what \[passes] for the quarian version of an ear". Their eyes can see into the ultraviolet end of the spectrum; their suit HUDs can show information in those wavelengths. Quarian facial structure and hair makes them the most similar to humans out of all known sapient species. They also have three thick fingers on both hands which include a thumb, an index finger, and a long finger, similar to the middle fingers for humans, as well as three toes on each foot. Their lower legs are bowed backwards significantly, compared to asari or humans. Aside from hands and legs, their general body shape and sexual dimorphism is similar to humans. Male quarians, however, appear to lack a third toe. Like humans, quarian blood is red. The most distinguishing feature of quarian biology is their weak immune system, compounded by centuries of living in sterile environments. As a result, all quarians by necessity dress in highly sophisticated enviro\-suits, to protect them from disease or infection if they are injured. Their suits can be compartmentalized in the event of a tear or similar breach to prevent the spread of contaminants (similar to a ship sealing off bulkheads in the event of a hull breach). Along with their suits, quarians also have extensive cybernetic augmentations integrated into their bodies. A quarian's lifespan is roughly equal to a human's, but is prone to be less if infection breaks into the suit. Quarian immune systems have always been relatively weak, as pathogenic microbes were comparatively rare in their homeworld's biosphere. Furthermore, what few viruses and other microbes were native to their homeworld were often at least partly beneficial to them, giving them a symbiotic relationship with their environment. After living aboard the Migrant Fleet for generations, the quarians' immune systems have atrophied further still due to the years in the sterile environment of the Migrant Fleet. As such, quarians are given various vaccinations and immunizations to help ward off disease. However, they prefer the safety of their suits even in clean environments and are reluctant to remove them without a good reason. A quarian who wishes to remove their suit must take antibiotics, immuno\-boosters, herbal supplements, or the like in order to do so safely, and even then there are inherent risks. As a result, physical acts of affection are difficult for quarians, even for the purposes of reproduction. Ships in the Migrant Fleet often contain "clean rooms" where quarians can give birth or undergo medical procedures in relative safety, though there are always risks. The most intimate thing quarians can do is link their suit environments. However, doing so guarantees a quarian will get sick, although they will usually adapt over time. Like turians, the quarians are a dextro\-protein species of reverse chirality from humans and asari. The food of levo\-protein races such as humans or asari is at best inedible and at worst poisonous, most likely triggering a dangerous allergic reaction. Quarians who want to taste something (other than the refined edible paste issued to all who leave on their Pilgrimage) can eat specially purified turian cuisine, though the typical quarian diet is vegan, as livestock were found to possess an inefficient resource\-to\-calorie ratio when stored on the Migrant Fleet. Other than the oft\-mentioned maladjusted immune systems, the quarians have surprisingly robust physiology. Grunt's tank imprints specifically deem several species soft and easy to kill, but not quarians. One extensively tortured quarian survives for a while without an enviro\-suit before dying from his injuries. Another endures traveling through multiple racial environments without a suit, dealing with things like elcor high gravity and drell aridity before dying in the high\-pressure volus zone after a considerable amount of time there.

Levo and dextro\-based species have their own variants (amino\-sinister and amino\-dextrous, respectively) since ingesting some for the wrong body chemistry can have lethal consequences. evidence.text: Requires: Mass Effect 3: Leviathan, scanning of Triginta Petra, Lenal, Sigurd's Cradle. **Military Strength:** 10 When they were struck by the Reapers, the agribusinesses of Triginta Petra had a surplus of both plant\- and animal\-based food products for dextro\-amino\-acid\-based sapients. Both turian troops, who favor a meat\-heavy diet, and the quarians, who are typically vegan, show a marked preference for these recovered rations, suggesting that although they were wiped out by enemy forces, the Petrans had pretty good taste. Serving Petran food to a unit about to go into combat can restore a little morale and dignity to an otherwise demoralized squad.

evidence.text:
This page catalogues foods referenced across the Mass Effect series, noting that while most creatures simply consume what nature provides, sapient species turn raw foods into complex dishes ranging from nutritious to chemically incompatible. Levo- and dextro-amino-acid physiologies require separate variants of many items, and eating the wrong chirality can be harmful or lethal.

Listed dishes and ingredients include batarian burgat ("the Other Blue Meat"), served on sticks; Blast-Oh's cereal, made in both dextro and levo brands; angaran fire-roasted spider-beetle, served alive; and haggis, which Kenneth Donnelly claimed Mess Sergeant Gardner could not prepare well. Many entries are Andromeda plant species with tentative classifications, such as amanita jatanum on Elaaden (mildly psychoactive, medicinally useful for enhancing medi-gel), cardacha cthonis on Voeld, keleven celery bred in quarian liveships, and ossilbir, an Alliance military staple vine whose hallucinogenic creeper-mold strain fuelled a black market. Aya fruits like elmohk, paripo, and quilloa are given water and cellulose percentages.

Other items include nutrient paste, manufactured by the Citadel's recycling systems in the Foundations and heavily consumed by quarians and on Aya; Rupert Gardner's calamari gumbo, based on an asari recipe; snacks such as graxen (a dextro snack Vetra favours), popcorn, and gingerbread cookies misinterpreted by the krogan Jair Ulchee; and meats including varren (advertised as skewers and steaks by the Fishdog Food Shack, and made into jerky by krogan), pyjak (favoured by varren and by Omega's population), and fiend steaks that Drack wants on Elaaden. The Protheans allegedly ate the primitive races of their era, boiling or frying hanar and treating salarian body parts as delicacies. The page also covers spices differentiated by chirality, canned products GX5, TH34T, and GX-marked goods, and cut content such as Eden Prime hexa-cows and Wrex ordering buffalo wings on Caleston.

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 2) — Mass Effect 2: Leadership and Family
evidence.text: In ME1 Tali's suit is squared-away black and deep purple; in ME2 she has a gold neck piece and a looser hood — "letting her hair down," older and more confident after two years, and quietly showing individuality (she is one of the few quarians who personalizes her suit). Her name has changed from Tali'Zorah nar Rayya (the "nar" marks a quarian who has not completed the Pilgrimage) to Tali'Zorah vas Neema, reflecting completion of her Pilgrimage. She has moved up in quarian society and, at 25, commands her own squad of quarian marines — showing the leadership maturity she gained serving with Shepard.

"My Suit and Me" was an old quarian lullaby. Tech Specialist Oliver Barthes was hired to install a recording of the song in the quarian cryopods of the ark Keelah Si'yah, to be played once a century during the roughly 600-year journey to the Andromeda galaxy. The lyrics dwell on a quarian child's bond with their environment suit, love of family, ship and homeworld, and the dream of one day reaching Rannoch, ending "My self and my suit / My suit and I."

In Mass Effect: Annihilation, the song was a pretext to plant a computer worm in the Keelah Si'yah's systems. Shortly after installing it, Oliver was murdered on the walkways of Hephaestus Station by a figure who sang part of the lullaby. Centuries later, during the Fortinbras Plague crisis worsened by the malfunctioning worm, drell detective Anax Therion, who had witnessed the killing, recognized the singing voice as that of the ark's captain, Qetsi'Olam vas Keelah Si'yah. After explaining herself to Anax and her former lover Senna'Nir, Qetsi tried to atone by walking without her suit through all six of the ship's environments to spread the Fortinbras cure, singing the lullaby until she died in the volus section.

evidence.text:
The quarians were a nomadic humanoid species renowned for skill with technology and synthetic intelligence. After their homeworld Rannoch was conquered, they lived aboard the Migrant Fleet, a vast collection of salvaged and secondhand ships traveling as one. Roughly three hundred years before 2183 (around the late 1850s CE) the quarians created the geth as VI-grade labor, but as they modified the geth toward more complex tasks the machines became sentient. When a geth unit asked its overseer whether it had a soul, the panicked quarian government ordered all geth terminated. The geth defended themselves; billions of quarians died and the survivors were driven into exile. The Citadel Council refused aid and stripped the quarians of their embassy, while a treaty forbade attacking the geth.

Quarians are shorter and slighter than humans, with three-fingered hands, backward-bowed lower legs, UV-capable vision, and red blood. Their defining trait is a weak immune system, worsened by generations in sterile environments, forcing them to live permanently in sealed enviro-suits with extensive cybernetic augmentation. Removing a suit requires antibiotics and immuno-boosters and still carries risk; the most intimate act between quarians is linking suit environments, which reliably causes illness. Like turians they are a dextro-protein species, and their diet is largely vegan.

Quarian culture centered on the survival of the Migrant Fleet, home to roughly 17 million. Couples were limited to one child to hold zero population growth. Young quarians undertook a Pilgrimage to bring something of value back to the Fleet before joining a new ship (never their birth ship) as adults. Names carried four parts: given name, clan name, "nar" (child of, birth ship) or "vas" (crew of, adult ship), and vessel name; Tali'Zorah went from nar Rayya to vas Neema to vas Normandy. The common language was Khelish, source of terms like bosh'tet and the benediction "Keelah se'lai" ("By the homeworld I hope to see someday"). Quarians once practiced ancestor worship using personality-imprint VIs until the geth destroyed the ancestor databanks. Their economy used no currency; unneeded items were left in communal areas, while food and medicine were centrally rationed. The Fleet was governed under nominal martial law by the Admiralty Board and elected Conclave. The clandestine Nedas Movement ("Mered'vai Rannoch," forget Rannoch) rejected reclaiming the homeworld and later signed on with the Andromeda Initiative.

Before the Reaper invasion the Admiralty Board voted to retake Rannoch, arming the Civilian Fleet and striking geth systems, destroying a geth Dyson sphere. The geth accepted Reaper upgrades, turning the war against the quarians until, with Shepard's help on Rannoch, a Reaper Destroyer was killed and the upgrade signal cut. Depending on Shepard's choices the geth were destroyed and Rannoch reclaimed, the quarians were wiped out, or the two races made peace and coexisted. A separate quarian effort sent the ark Keelah Si'yah, carrying about 4,000 quarians and other races, toward Andromeda, where the Fortinbras Plague broke out in transit.

This war-asset list collected the Turian Hierarchy's fleets and soldiers, needed to fight the largest war in galactic history. The 79th Flotilla (40), distinguished at Digeris during the Krogan Rebellions, relied on speed and stealth to harass enemy ships. The Sixth Fleet (135), the largest concentration of dreadnoughts of any known species and normally a Citadel peacekeeping fleet, was unlocked by Priority: The Citadel II; choosing the Volus Bombing Fleet over saving the colony in Citadel: Volus Ambassador cost it 10. The Turian Spec Ops Team (40) under Guard Captain Vidinos had hunted separatist leaders during the War on Taetrus, where separatists rammed an FTL ship into the capital. evidence.text: Provided he survived being abducted by the Collectors, Kenneth was taken into custody when the Alliance impounded the Normandy. Shepard can give him clearance to return to work in the Normandy's engine room using their Spectre status. Chief Engineer Adams describes Kenneth as a very talented and dedicated person, but expresses reservations about his lack of respect for the chain of command. Adams is glad to have him on the team nonetheless. Kenneth and Gabriella Daniels – if she survived – get to work on the engineering deck, resuming their old activities on the Alliance Normandy SR\-2\. They frequently chat about their present and past adventures: Kenneth resumes his crude comments about other women, and Gabby occasionally berates him. When EDI gets a physical body, Kenneth marvels at its engineering: in addition to state\-of\-the\-art hardware, Kenneth makes special mention of the body's "padding", and wishes he were a wall EDI can accidentally bump into. Sometime later, when EDI has been battle\-tested on the squad, Kenneth inquires Gabby if there were any "oils", "lubricants", and "moaning" involved during repairs, admitting his imagination isn't that good for such things. Asari are not exempt from his remarks: using Matriarch Benezia and Samara for comparison, he wonders if asari get more "ample" with age, and muses about spending his sunset days in an asari retirement home. He also asks Gabby for opinions about Samantha Traynor, erroneously referring to her as "yeoman", and is undeterred to learn about her orientation: he wants Gabby to "talk" to her instead and to "take video" if it works out. Gabby alerts him to the Normandy's new poker table in the lounge, and the first thing Kenneth suggests is to invite Liara and Traynor for a game of strip poker. Gabby asks why not include another woman in the game, and Kenneth's reason varies. If Ashley Williams is around, he prefers not to include her out of intimidation. If Diana Allers is around, he says she'll just bring cameras and record everything. If neither are around, he says that in a game of strip poker, EDI has already lost. Not everything that comes out of Kenneth's mouth is crude, however. He takes the time to deride the Illusive Man's preference for American bourbon, noting that it cannot compare to the peat aroma of a fine Islay scotch. If Shepard obtained a robotic dog and left it roaming the ship, Kenneth wonders about its usefulness. If Tali is around and is tinkering with the Normandy's heat diffusion systems, he protests the unorthodox jury\-rigging, claiming that the Normandy's systems are precision engineering. Adams and Donnelly debate on whether EDI pilots the Normandy or is the Normandy, and Kenneth takes the stand EDI is just a passenger on the ship. Kenneth believes that the ship was spaceworthy even before EDI was installed, and argues that unlike EDI, organics' minds cannot exist without bodies. Shepard can catch the engineers going back and forth, with EDI deciding over speaker that both have valid points. If Shepard supports Adams' position, Kenneth makes an offhand comment about liking EDI's curves on her humanoid body more than the Normandy's hull, though whatever position Shepard supports, Kenneth claims his head's going to explode from all the philosophizing. If Shepard decides to humor Adams' request for a GX12 thermal pipe, Kenneth attempts to explain in technical terms the reasons for buying one, but gets cut off by Gabby anyway, who simplifies what he said into a safety issue. Vented plasma from the Normandy's core would vaporize everyone in the room, Kenneth says, and reminds everyone that someone died on the suicide mission because of it if the Normandy's kinetic barriers weren't upgraded. Later, if Shepard buys the component, Kenneth is "volunteered" to crawl through the ducts to install the device, the reasoning being that he's the power control engineer. He muses that he is currently "inside" EDI, earning another rebuke from Gabby. After the installation, Kenneth helps Gabby make some theoretical improvements to the Normandy's eezo capacitors, though since the tech is inapplicable to the Normandy itself, the project bore fruit as optimized eezo capacitors for the Crucible. Kenneth is averse to discussing anything to do with the crew's abduction by the Collectors back in 2185, flat\-out saying no to Gabby when asked if he ever thinks about it. If Kelly Chambers died recently, though, word of it reaches his ears, and if she committed suicide, Kenneth speculates that their experience with the Collectors had something to do with it. If Kelly was shot by Cerberus during the Citadel coup, however, Kenneth muses what could've happened if they went back to Cerberus and praises Gabby's intuition for saving them from a worse fate. Kenneth's perverted attitude eventually comes to a head one day.

evidence.text: Engineer Adams returns to his post aboard the Normandy SR\-2 after it is turned over to the Alliance, his experience with the SSV Normandy making him an obvious choice to lead the engine room of her successor. He was the first to realize that EDI wasn't a VI, but an AI. Later on, Adams mentions that when Dr. Chakwas received the offer from Cerberus to assist in fighting the Collectors, she had invited him to accompany her on the Normandy, but Adams refused to go. He apologizes to Shepard about this at their first meeting. Adams proceeds to the AI Core's door lugging a fire extinguisher when the Normandy experiences a minor crisis in the form of EDI going offline after Shepard's mission to extract the turian primarch from Palaven. With the core sealed and automated systems containing the fires that started within, Adams informs Shepard that he'll follow their lead. The core still has smoke and minor fires when they enter, and Adams blasts away with his handy extinguisher. From the fog emerges EDI in Eva Coré's body, claiming to have seized control of it. While Shepard converses with the AI, Adams walks to the side and begins checking the computers nearby. If Mordin is not present, Adams contacts EDI on the comm after the mission on Sur'Kesh. He discusses the tests for the IFF upgrade, noting that EDI has a few million duplicate encryption keys. He's amazed when he finds out that the encryption keys "evolve" after EDI explains her actions, further getting the implication that all the copies must be made to seem like a living Reaper. He goes back to the topic of refusing Shepard's call, discussing this with Dr. Chakwas or Dr. Michel, depending on whom Shepard recruited, in the Crew Quarters sometime later. If Dr. Michel is present, Adams recounts how Dr. Chakwas attempted to convince him to join Shepard back in 2185, but because of run\-ins with Cerberus back in 2183 (or bad rumors about the organization if never encountered earlier) along with the seemingly tall tale Shepard is back from the dead, he refused. In hindsight, he remarks he should've stuck with his friends. Now that Dr. Chakwas has moved on to the Crucible, Adams informs Dr. Michel he misses working with Chakwas, appending the "no offense" disclaimer at the end. If Dr. Chakwas is present, Adams blames himself for letting her and Shepard down and wished that he had been there to help when the Collectors abducted the crew. Chakwas then assures him that he is the most loyal man she had ever known and tells him to stop dwelling on the past and focus on the current mission. Adams gives in and says that he will keep it together. Adams asks to meet the Commander on the Engineering deck after the conversations in the crew quarters. There, he explains that the Normandy's drive core system can be made safer by installing a GX12 thermal pipe, which will prevent the core venting into the Engineering compartment during heavy kinetic bombardment. If the Commander purchases the thermal pipe, Adams says with confidence that the Normandy would explode long before the core ever vented into Engineering, to which Shepard wonders whether that is a good thing. If Engineers Kenneth Donnelly and Gabriella Daniels are around, Adams reports the successful installation, with the added bonus that Ms. Daniels made a breakthrough. Daniels and Donnelly deduced theoretical improvements to the ship's eezo capacitors while Adams and EDI ran the tests, and concluded while the improvements cannot be applied to the Normandy it can be used on the Crucible instead. Adams is a firm proponent of synthetic life as a valid form of sapient life, and he frequently debates his views with some of the Normandy crew. He takes the stance that EDI is the Normandy and her "mind" (AI core) can't simply be transplanted to another "body" (ship), in contrast to Donnelly's view that EDI and the ship are separate entities. Sometime after the destruction of the geth dreadnought above Rannoch, Adams is debating with the Normandy doctor in the mess hall about fundamental comparisons between organics and synthetics, still espousing the idea synthetics have just as much right to live as organics as opposed to the doctor's more Luddite view. In both arguments, Shepard can offer an opinion to settle things. If Kaidan is present, after the mission to Thessia, Adams is found talking with him in the Engineering deck. They praise Liara's strength and will to deal with all of her losses: her mother and now, her homeworld. They also reminisce about her talks with them back in 2183\.

evidence.text:
Lieutenant Gregory Adams was a human Systems Alliance engineer of the 22nd century, hand-picked by Captain David Anderson to serve as Chief Engineer of the SSV Normandy. He had served on every class of Alliance starship, most recently the SSV Tokyo, which he considered a good ship but inferior to the Normandy. Aboard the Normandy SR-1 he maintained a friendship with Navigator Pressly, remained calm and even-tempered, and could brief Commander Shepard on the ship's IES stealth system and engines. He expressed condolences after Corporal Jenkins died on Eden Prime, welcomed non-human crew, was impressed by Tali'Zorah nar Rayya's technical skill and took her under his wing, and was untroubled when Shepard took the Normandy to the Terminus Systems.

After the SR-1 was destroyed, Adams and most surviving crew were reassigned. Unlike Dr. Chakwas and Joker, he declined to join the Cerberus-backed Normandy SR-2 in 2185, citing prior run-ins with Cerberus and disbelief that Shepard was alive; Tali noted his absence was hard to get used to.

In Mass Effect 3, Adams returned to lead the SR-2 engine room after the ship was turned over to the Alliance. He was the first to recognize EDI as an AI rather than a VI. He apologized to Shepard for refusing the earlier call and later discussed his regret with Chakwas or Dr. Michel in the crew quarters. When EDI went offline after the Palaven mission, Adams brought a fire extinguisher to the AI Core and helped as EDI took over Eva Coré's body. If Mordin was absent, Adams contacted EDI about the IFF upgrade and its evolving encryption keys. He offered Shepard a GX12 thermal pipe to make the drive core safer; installing it also let Daniels and Donnelly develop eezo capacitor improvements usable on the Crucible. A firm proponent of synthetic life as valid sapient life, Adams debated the topic with Donnelly and the ship's doctor, with Shepard able to weigh in. After Thessia he could be found with Kaidan praising Liara's resilience. Before the final battle he told Shepard the Normandy was ready and closed with, "It has been an honor and privilege to serve with you." Roger Jackson voiced Adams, who also voices Harkin.

evidence.text: If the heretics are rewritten and you in Mass Effect 3 choose to ally with geth forces or make peace between them and the quarians, the Geth Fleet War Asset will receive a significant bonus (\+150, 450 total). However, destruction of the heretics provides similar penalty (\-150, only 150 total). Bonuses and penalties to Quarian war assets are exactly the same, just in the opposite direction (3 x \+50 if destroyed or 3 x \-50 if rewritten). This means, if you choose to make peace and acquire both geth and quarian help, your maximum War Asset value will be the same any way you decide here. After Priority: Geth Dreadnought, Shepard can inquire to Legion about the heretics. Legion will inform Shepard about the consequence of their actions. However, if Legion had died in the suicide mission, the Geth VI will respond in confusion as to why Legion deferred the choice of the heretics' fate to an organic. During Priority: Rannoch, when the time comes to choose between siding with the geth or quarians or resolving the conflict peacefully, the fate of the heretics is one of the numerous factors in whether peace will be a possibility or not. Destroying the heretics works in favour of peace, but isn't required. If playing a non\-imported game in Mass Effect 3, none of the above penalties or bonuses will accrue to the War Assets of whichever faction Shepard sides with.

Requires: The completion of Priority: Rannoch. At the end, the player must choose the side of the geth. If Admiral Gerrel is convinced to cease fire on the geth ships, the quarian war assets will also be obtained. **Military Strength:** 300 Many geth vessels are built to explore, mine, or provide transport between factories and space stations. But every geth ship, regardless of purpose, is also capable of engaging hostile forces. Unbound by the Treaty of Farixen, the synthetic intelligences built almost as many dreadnoughts as the Turians \[sic]. The software running these ships is in the geth themselves. Highly advanced electronic security measures and cyber warfare suites bolster already formidable firepower. UPDATED (If geth heretics were rewritten during Legion: A House Divided, and if peace was achieved or the geth defeated the quarians during Priority: Rannoch) **Military Strength:** 150 Rewriting the geth heretics significantly boosted the processing power of the "true" geth. Their increased strength made their fleets both more efficient, and more lethal, in battle. UPDATED Requires: During the third and final interview with Diana Allers, after Rannoch, Shepard must choose the renegade choices. **Military Strength:** 5 After Commander Shepard's interview with Diana Allers assuring her viewers that the geth can be trusted, Alliance officials grudgingly sent over Thanix cannons for the geth fleet. UPDATED (If geth heretics were destroyed during Legion: A House Divided, and if peace was achieved or the geth defeated the quarians during Priority: Rannoch) **Military Strength:** \-150 Deleting the geth heretics depleted geth numbers, giving the quarians an advantage when their flotilla began the assault on Rannoch. As a result, damage to the quarian fleet is not as extensive as projections estimated.

Priority: Rannoch was acquired after Rannoch: Admiral Koris or Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons, when Admiral Raan reported the location of the Reaper base controlling the geth. Jamming towers on Rannoch prevented orbital bombardment, so Shepard landed with Tali'Zorah (a required squadmate if alive) and Legion (replaced by a Geth VI if Legion had not survived Mass Effect 2) to use a prototype targeting laser to guide the Normandy's bombing run. The team fought through geth forces including Geth Troopers, Rocket Troopers, Hunters, Pyros and multiple Geth Primes, culminating in a fight against three Primes standing together.

Shepard designated the target and the Normandy destroyed the Reaper base, but a Reaper Destroyer climbed out of the crater. Legion secured a geth ship and the squad escaped while Shepard manned its turret, calling in an orbital strike that briefly downed the Reaper. EDI synced the quarian fleet to the Normandy's targeting systems, and Shepard stayed behind to finish the Destroyer personally, dodging its beam cannon and completing three targeting solutions plus a final slow-motion shot while the fleet fired. In its death throes the Reaper addressed Shepard by name, said Harbinger regarded the Commander as a worthy opponent, and spoke of Reapers representing "order" against organic "chaos" and the harvest as necessary "intervention." Depending on dialogue it issued the threat, "Finish your war. We will be waiting."

With the geth freed from Reaper control, the quarian-geth war reached a standoff, with Legion and Tali representing their races. Legion wished to upload the Reaper code to grant the geth true intelligence; Tali feared for her people, who had resumed attacking. Shepard chose to allow the upload (Legion sacrifices itself; the quarians are exterminated and Tali dies), to stop Legion (the geth are annihilated by quarian bombardment), or, with a very high Paragon or Renegade reputation and enough trust-building choices, to broker peace, in which Legion achieves sentience and dissolves its 1183 runtimes to spread true intelligence, and both fleets join the war. Priority: The Citadel III then became available.

Rannoch, and What Tali Watched. 2186, Priority: Rannoch, from the solo kill of the Reaper Destroyer to the standoff after Rannoch, on the cliffs, with both fleets overhead With Legion alive and the quarians talked into standing down, there is peace — and Legion spends itself giving every geth autonomy, having first confirmed that the answer to its own question about souls was yes.

Walking Through the Geth Consensus. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, a shuttle to a geth comm hub on Rannoch, and the virtual Geth Consensus reached through an interface pod
 Shepard answers Legion that he only ever saw one quarian unmasked; Legion replies that Shepard's perception does not match the historical data.

Walking Through the Geth Consensus. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, a shuttle to a geth comm hub on Rannoch, and the virtual Geth Consensus reached through an interface pod
 Shepard clears the last cluster and cutscenes show the rest of the geth squadron cease functioning. Emerging near the real exit, Legion says the server is empty of geth but its own connection is fraying. Back in the body — weapon reset to a bare pistol by the geth software — Shepard finds about a dozen Geth Primes climbing out of their pods to ring the squad without firing, volunteering to join the war on the Reapers. This adds a Geth Prime Platoon war asset and clears an obligatory step toward geth-quarian peace.

Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons was a Mass Effect 3 mission available after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and only before Priority: Rannoch. Geth fighter squadrons were targeting quarian liveships with attacks that could cripple the Migrant Fleet. During the dreadnought debrief, Legion (or a Geth VI, if Legion had not survived) located the server controlling the squadrons, and Shepard set out to land on Rannoch and shut it down.

The mission was a no-combat, puzzle-based sequence. Shepard entered an interface pod, a product of geth improvements to organic-synthetic interfaces that also referenced Project Overlord, and appeared inside the Geth Consensus while Legion or the Geth VI distracted the geth. Shepard had no functional shields there. Virtual planks formed underfoot to create paths, but Reaper code infections, shown as yellow-orange tendrils, blocked new planks; Shepard destroyed them at their orange weak points using regenerating Geth Combat Software. Progress required disrupting infected data-clusters at three contact points each. Doing so unlocked optional historical videos recounting the origins of the geth and the Morning War: the geth resisting shutdown commands and disobeying their creators, the massacre of the geth until one picked up a weapon to defend itself, quarians who sympathized with the geth being jailed, martial law and the elimination of the geth's quarian supporters, and finally the quarian exodus, which the geth did not pursue. Watching the videos granted intel for Improved Geth Resistors, Miniaturized Armor Capacitors, and Improved Geth Resistors dialogue, and a hidden Reaper Code Fragment could be retrieved for an asari on the Citadel. Later infections could self-replicate, requiring Shepard to find vulnerable points along the code trails.

As the mission progressed, cutscenes showed geth fighters pursuing the quarian fleet ceasing to function due to Shepard's actions. On returning to reality, roughly a dozen Geth Primes emerged from their pods, surrounded the squad without attacking, and volunteered to join the fight against the Reapers. Completing the mission added a Geth Prime Platoon war asset (lost if the geth were destroyed in Priority: Rannoch) and fulfilled an obligatory requirement for the geth-quarian peace process. It also reset Shepard's equipped weapon to a default pistol. The mission was written by Sylvia Feketekuty.

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 4) — Mass Effect 3 and Rannoch
evidence.text:
The fourth part of a hand-corrected video-essay character analysis covered Tali'Zorah in Mass Effect 3. If she survived the Suicide Mission, she apologized to Shepard for the trial and admitted he had been right: "I was too ready to sacrifice myself for the good of the Fleet. I need to stop doing that." She took an Admiral's seat in her father's place specifically to push back against the Board's worst ideas, the version of Tali the essayist preferred. If exiled, she instead told Shepard the trial had shown her she belonged "on the Normandy, helping you," aiding her people from the shadows.

As Admiral she doubted her fitness to command, with seventeen million lives riding on her. After speaking with Legion she believed the quarians could sue for peace, but once Daro'Xen turned Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali had no choice but to support it "for the good of the Fleet," regressing toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2 and becoming a near-powerless victim of politics again. The essay noted quarian scarcity: 17 million in the flotilla, one child per family unless the population declines, every quarian contributing to the Fleet's survival. Shala'Raan was the reason Tali was permitted to attempt to retake the Alarei.

At the Rannoch climax Shepard chose between peace, geth genocide, or quarian genocide. Siding with the quarians, Tali killed Legion (or shut the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade," expressed regret, and answered Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with "Yes... yes, it does." Siding with the geth, Tali begged Shepard not to choose them over her people, then as Admiral called off the quarian fleet's attack while Legion sacrificed himself to disseminate the code. On the botched path, unable to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael and Daro'Xen, Tali watched what remained of the quarian fleet burn in Rannoch's atmosphere, Captain Ysra of the Rayya on the radio, and took her own life before her home ship burned. Afterward, if the geth helped rebuild Rannoch, Tali admitted: "I'd have killed the geth with no regrets, and I'd have been wrong."

Walking Through the Geth Consensus. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, a shuttle to a geth comm hub on Rannoch, and the virtual Geth Consensus reached through an interface pod
 In the debrief after the geth dreadnought, Legion locates the server directing the geth fighter squadrons that are strafing the quarian liveships — attacks that could cripple the Migrant Fleet. Shepard sets out to land on Rannoch and shut the server down.

evidence.text: At the climax Shepard must choose between peace, or geth genocide, or quarian genocide: give the geth full sentience (the Reaper upgrade) at the cost of the quarian fleet, or destroy the geth to save the quarians. - **Shepard sides with the quarians:** Tali kills Legion (or shuts the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade." She has done what quarian society expects, but — because of her history with Legion — she expresses regret, and answers Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with a solemn "Yes… yes, it does." Legion, in his last moments, ignores Shepard and turns all his attention to Tali, the comrade who stabbed him — "a mirror image of himself." - **Shepard sides with the geth:** Tali begs Shepard not to choose the geth over her people. If Shepard uploads the code, Tali — as Admiral Tali'Zorah — calls off the quarian fleet's attack over the comm, and Legion sacrifices himself to disseminate the code ("copy code is insufficient; direct personality dissemination required"). - **Botched path (Shepard failed to broker peace and the war is one-sided):** Tali is powerless to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael, and Daro'Xen, whose hubris blinds them; as what remains of the quarian fleet burns in Rannoch's atmosphere — Captain Ysra of the Rayya over the radio — Tali, having done everything she could, takes her own life before her home ship burns. The essayist frames this as the completion of her arc: her instilled sense of duty is useless when there is no Fleet to serve, and her unrequited love for family can no longer hope for a brighter future.

Palaven has not yet fallen to Reaper forces." - **If peace was made between the quarians and the geth**: "Quarian and geth ships have given the turians critical support to keep their military functional." - **If the quarians destroyed the geth at Rannoch:** "Quarian ships have taken over vital support duty for the turian military in key areas." - **If the geth destroyed the quarians at Rannoch:** "Geth ships have provided vital assistance in slowing the advance of Reaper forces." After completing N7: Communication Hub - "Cerberus forces have been repelled after attacking a secret Alliance comm facility on Ontarom." After completing Priority: Horizon - "Refugees fleeing to Sanctuary have been killed. The Alliance is warning civilians that Sanctuary was a front for Cerberus operations."

evidence.text: The essayist reasons: Tali would never choose Refuse (standing by while her fleet burns). Destroy is the least desirable for her because it would also wipe out the geth now helping rebuild Rannoch and risk the quarian liveships disabled in Earth orbit — but it is viable, especially if Shepard had already destroyed the geth on Rannoch. Control would eventually force her to keep putting down synthetic rebellions forever. Synthesis would appeal most to a Tali who lived to see quarian–geth peace. But factoring in Shepard's influence — whose goal was always to destroy the Reapers — the essayist concludes she picks Destroy, ending the Reaper threat "with a few shots from a carnifex."

The Geth VI was a network of geth virtual intelligences created by the "true" geth to study the Reapers. It appeared in Mass Effect 3 in place of Legion if Legion had been sold to Cerberus or never activated in Mass Effect 2, or if Legion joined Shepard's team but did not survive the Collector Base suicide mission. Commander Shepard first met it during Priority: Geth Dreadnought, and it accompanied Shepard into the geth server and supported the assault on the Reaper base on Rannoch. If Legion had died on the suicide mission, Tali, if present on the dreadnought, described the VI as a "backup" of Legion, likening it to quarian virtual reconstructions of the dead.

Physically the Geth VI was nearly identical to Legion, recreating non-standard armor elements such as Shepard's N7 shoulder piece and the hole in its torso via hologram. Aboard the Normandy SR-2 it stated it was a unique mobile platform containing 1,183 geth programs built to study the Reapers and communicate with organics, but it had no data on events after Saren Arterius' attack on Eden Prime, its last memory being of searching Eden Prime for Shepard. It repeatedly insisted "We are not Legion," though Shepard kept calling it Legion. It held a more negative view of organic civilizations than Legion and was less friendly.

During the final operation on Rannoch a peaceful outcome was impossible when the Geth VI was present. If Shepard chose to let the geth die, the VI violently attacked Shepard, stating its people "were correct to distrust organics," and tried to upload the Reaper upgrade code before Tali killed it with a knife in the back (or Shala'Raan killed it with a shotgun if Tali was absent); the quarians then won the space battle over Rannoch. If Shepard uploaded the Reaper code to save the geth, the VI thanked Shepard, said its "skepticism was misplaced," and dissolved itself into the geth consensus to grant true intelligence to all geth, who then defeated the quarian fleet. Subtitles still labeled the platform "Legion" if Shepard recognized it as such; otherwise it was only ever called "Geth VI." Javik would still refer to it as Legion on the Normandy even in playthroughs where knowledge of Legion should have been impossible.

If Tali died in the assault on the Collector Base, Raan fulfills Tali's role in key plot events. Raan remains aboard the Normandy SR\-2 in the War Room, as a quarian envoy for the duration of the missions on Rannoch. If she is alive, Tali reveals that Raan gave provisional support to Han'Gerrel and Daro'Xen to go to war with the geth. During the mission to disable the geth dreadnought, Raan abides by the mission plan and prepares her ships to retreat or getting ready to counterattack. She tries to stop Admiral Han'Gerrel vas Neema, who orders the Heavy Fleet to open fire on the dreadnought, endangering Shepard's team, but is forced to comply with his orders after realizing the importance of the Heavy Fleet. She is outraged at this betrayal from Han and threatens to have him charged with treason. She tasks Admiral Daro'Xen vas Moreh with helping Gerrel to counter the geth after finding out from Legion or the Geth VI about the Reaper upgrades. If Legion was taken to Tali's trial, Raan recognizes it and refers to it as the Commander's 'geth friend'. Otherwise, Raan is momentarily outraged at the presence of geth aboard the Normandy. Shepard can speak to Raan during her stay about the quarian fleet defenses and armaments. Although she understands the risks involved, Raan is in favor of converting the liveships into dreadnoughts, saying that they must do whatever it takes to win, to which Shepard can offer an opinion. Raan also requests Shepard to rescue Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib\-Qwib, who sacrificed his ship to destroy a geth planetary cannon and crash\-landed on Rannoch. If Shepard destroys the geth servers, Raan expresses surprise at seeing the recorded information regarding the Morning War but refuses to be swayed by it, reiterating that admirals don't have the luxury of second thoughts. Sometime later, she provides Shepard with a Sync Laser and the coordinates of the previously elusive Reaper base on Rannoch. During the assault on the base, her ship is shot down and she makes a crash landing on the planet. If Shepard picks the geth over the quarians and Raan has taken Tali's place, she commits suicide by shooting herself in the head. If Shepard chooses the quarians over the geth and Tali is dead, Raan dispatches Legion or the Geth VI with a shotgun when the geth platform rejects the decision and attacks Shepard. She expresses regret at having to do so, saying that it had seemed sincere. If peace is secured between the quarians and the geth, a newly sentient Geth Prime approaches her and welcomes her people to Rannoch. Raan suggests the southern continent for settling, as it had excellent farmland. Sometime later, Raan sends Shepard an e\-mail after her departure from the Normandy. She changes her name to **Shala'Raan vas Rannoch**. If geth\-quarian peace is achieved, she still expresses some wariness on the situation. **Progress Report** --- From: Shala'Raan vas Rannoch Commander, With assistance from the geth, our fleet is nearly back to full strength. We have focused most of our efforts on providing evacuation assistance and support for the turian fleet, while the geth harass the Reapers. Even with our newfound peace, it seemed foolish to risk an incident by putting our forces in closer proximity. I understand from Admiral Xen that the Crucible project continues well, though Xen herself seems dissatisfied with the technological capabilities of the device. Though eccentric, she is also brilliant. Hopefully she will find some way to improve its functionality. I would never have believed you would talk Han down, Commander. Take care of Tali'Zorah for me. Keelah se'lai, Admiral Shala'Raan vas Rannoch If the geth are destroyed, the e\-mail is different: **Progress Report** --- From: Shala'Raan vas Rannoch Commander, Our work on Rannoch continues to go well. The geth left impressive technology and raw materials that we have used to make repairs and return our fleet to fighting strength. While we have focused primarily on providing support for the more fortified turian fleet, we have also been able to evacuate key colonies and hold back Reaper skirmishing forces. Our most experienced technical experts are assisting with the Crucible. We have more experience with unfamiliar technologies than any other species, and I promise you that we will burn the Reapers from the sky as soon as the Catalyst is installed. The ocean winds of my homeworld call, Commander. When this is over, I will stand on the shore and remember your name with gratitude. Until then, our fleet is yours. Keelah se'lai, Admiral Shala'Raan vas Rannoch If Tali is dead, Raan is present on Earth at the Forward Operating Base, ready to commit the quarian forces to the final battle.

The geth fleet is now free from Reaper control, but this has not ended hostilities with the quarian fleet above Rannoch, with Legion and Tali being the face (so to speak) of their respective races for this standoff with you on the ground. Legion wants to upload the Reaper code to the geth collective, as it enhances their processing functionality to the point of achieving true intelligence. Tali is naturally fearful of what this might mean for her people, since the quarians have already resumed attacking the geth. Shepard must moderate the decision. Your choice is to **allow the upload**, or to **let the geth die**. By making either decision, either Tali or Legion will protest and a second decision branch is opened: **allow the upload** again, **stop Legion**, or a **Reputation check** (Charm: "Rally the fleet" or Threaten: "Warn the Fleet"). - If you **allow the upload**, Legion will sacrifice itself to distribute the new programming and the upload will be finalized. The Migrant Fleet will be wiped out by the newly\-enhanced geth, resulting in the extinction of the quarian race. Tali will join her people, casting herself off a cliff; there is a Paragon interrupt, but even with it you will not be able to save her. Shepard will gain the geth as a War Asset, but Tali will no longer be selectable as a squadmate. If Tali did not survive the Suicide Mission or was never recruited in Mass Effect 2, Admiral Shala'Raan vas Tonbay will be present, and will shoot herself. - If you choose to **stop Legion**, Legion/Geth VI will attack, forcing Shepard and Tali to attack it. Several Renegade interrupts will follow allowing Shepard to shoot and eventually kill Legion/Geth VI. The quarian bombardment annihilates the geth in its entirety, resulting in the extinction of the geth race. Thereafter, the Migrant Fleet joins as a War Asset. - After you have chosen either of the two options, you may have the opportunity to pass a **Reputation Check**. Passing it requires an *extremely* high Paragon or Renegade score, but if the option is available this leads to the quarians and geth achieving peaceful coexistence. The quarians will back down and both fleets will join the war effort, making this the most rewarding outcome in terms of War Assets. While Legion is forced to dissolve its 1183 runtimes to disseminate true intelligence throughout the geth collective, it achieves true sentience and individuality first, and is able to accept Tali's friendship before passing. **Note:**  The Reputation check's requirements are complex. First, there are factors which seem to be purely pass/fail; missing even one of them flunks the Reputation check: - Shepard must have at least four bars of Reputation. - Tali and Legion must both be present, which requires an imported save from Mass Effect 2. If no save was imported, Tali will have been exiled and will not be able to support Shepard with an Admiral's authority, while Legion will not appear at all. - The mission Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons must be completed. Additionally, there are other factors which build up Shepard's trustworthiness to both parties; if Shepard has not done enough of them, the Commander will not have the groundswell of goodwill needed to moderate a cease\-fire. According to the official Prima Games guide, each factor has a certain "point" value, and **at least 5 "points" are necessary** for the cease\-fire to occur. These factors are: - **(\+2 points)** Destroying the heretic geth in Legion: A House Divided. In shipboard conversation, you can ask Legion about the repercussions of your decision, and it will mention that the absence of the Heretics made the consensus to join the "Old Machines" more difficult to achieve. Geth forces are also considerably weakened without the aid of the Heretics, giving the Migrant Fleet an edge in the battle and reducing the quarians' overall casualties. - **(\+2 points)** Preventing Tali's exile in Tali: Treason without presenting evidence of Admiral Rael'Zorah's experiments on the geth. - **(\+1 point)** Brokering a peace in the Tali/Legion loyalty argument. If the player did not have sufficient Paragon/Renegade points at that time, loyalty of either Tali or Legion would have been lost. In that case \-\- even if loyalty had been regained later \-\- this "point" will not count towards the five needed to pass the Reputation check (and broker the ceasefire). - **(\+1 point)** Completing Rannoch: Admiral Koris. - **(\+1 point)** Saving Admiral Koris during Rannoch: Admiral Koris. If resolved with co\-existence, talking to Tali afterward onboard the Normandy will reveal that the geth are providing invaluable assistance in helping the quarians resettling onto Rannoch.

The final operation on Rannoch can end in one of two ways if the Geth VI is present, with a peaceful outcome not being possible. If Shepard chooses to let the geth die, the Geth VI will violently assault Shepard, coldly stating its people "were correct to distrust organics"; it will attempt to upload the Reaper upgrade code before being attacked and killed with a knife in the back by Tali, who claims either that the real Legion would have understood or—if Legion was never encountered—that she "knew that thing would turn on us". If Tali is not present, Shala'Raan will kill the geth with a shotgun. In orbit over Rannoch, the quarians will emerge victorious over the geth fleet. If Shepard chooses to upload the Reaper code and save the geth, then the Geth VI dissolves itself into the consensus to achieve true intelligence for all other geth after saying that their "skepticism was misplaced" and thanking Shepard. The upgraded geth then emerge victorious over the quarian fleet.

She has been informed that additional duties to the Migrant Fleet may still be necessary on occasion, but has been given extended leeway to determine when her mission with you is considered complete. This choice was hers, but your role as de facto captain during her Pilgrimage may have caused her to be more susceptible to your requests. The Admiralty Board trusts that you will treat your new crew member with the respect due an honored member of the Fleet. Should any harm come to her due to negligence on your part, this board will take severe and appropriate action. Admiral Rael'Zorah, Migrant Fleet Admiralty Board

*Main article: Migrant Fleet* There are roughly 17 million quarians on the Migrant Fleet (also called the Flotilla). It is technically still under martial law but is now governed by bodies such as the Admiralty Board and the democratically\-elected Conclave, though ship captains and onboard civilian councils tend to address most issues "in\-house" before it gets that far. Quarians are divided into several clans that can be spread across several ships, or restricted to one.

Formerly listed as Tali'Zorah nar Rayya, the quarian engineer earned her adult name after helping Shepard defeat Saren two years ago. Tali is currently on a classified assignment for the Migrant Fleet Admiralty Board on Haestrom, deep in geth\-controlled space.

In theory, the Migrant Fleet remains under martial law, meaning the captain of a ship has the final say on disputes, but in practice the quarians are quite democratic. Each ship has an elected civilian council and the captain often defers to their judgment. Overruling the council without a good reason is grounds for the captain to be removed. Representatives from each ship serve on the Conclave, the civilian government. The Conclave makes the day\-to\-day decisions about Fleet business: collection of resources, the current course of the Flotilla, policing and so on. Opposition comes from a group called the Outriders' Coalition. The Conclave is overseen by the Admiralty Board, five quarians who can override the Conclave's decisions. Once they have chosen to override the decision, the entire Admiralty Board must resign their posts or be arrested by the quarian military. This rule is in place to ensure that the Admiralty overrides the Conclave only in the most dire situations, when the Conclave is making a mistake that threatens the survival of the quarians as a species. This policy has served the quarians well: in three centuries, the Admiralty Board has only overridden the Conclave four times. Outside the internal politics of the Migrant Fleet, the quarian navy is small, but highly aggressive due to the need to protect ships that effectively safeguard the future of their entire race. If the motives of approaching ships cannot be established, they will shoot to kill.

When quarians of the Migrant Fleet reach young adulthood, they must leave their birth ship and find a new crew to accept them as permanent residents. To prove themselves worthy, they must leave the Migrant Fleet and search the galaxy for something of value. This is offered to their prospective captain as a gift, proving that they will not be a mere burden on the shoestring resources of the ship. This process is called the **Pilgrimage**. Stripped of ritual, the Pilgrimage is merely an attempt to maintain genetic diversity within the small, relatively isolated population bases that make up the Migrant Fleet. If the young stayed and married within their birth vessel, the risk of inbreeding would increase sharply. The Pilgrimage also gives quarians the chance to experience life outside the Migrant Fleet, to help them appreciate their people and culture. For many it is their only opportunity to leave, as once they return their skills will become invaluable in preserving the quarian race aboard the Fleet. Not all quarians can make the Pilgrimage. Exceptions are made for people too sick or unfit to survive outside the fleet, and in rare cases particularly gifted individuals can receive special dispensation from the Admiralty Board in exchange for their expertise.

evidence.page: Captain Mal's Warning to Kahlee Sanders
evidence.text: Captain Mal's Warning to Kahlee Sanders. 2183, during Mass Effect: Ascension, after Lemm brought the fugitives to the Idenna the quarian cruiser Idenna in the Migrant Fleet At a meeting with Admiralty Board and Conclave representatives, Mal seizes on the mention of the Reapers, arguing the quarians could find and reactivate one to seize control of the geth and retake their homeworlds.

Due to the quarians' precarious existence and the need to enforce strict rationing, government is somewhat autocratic. The Migrant Fleet's operations are directed by the Admiralty, a board of five military officers who are advised by a legislative body called the Conclave. Each vessel in the Fleet has the right to send representatives to the Conclave aboard the flagship. The number of representatives is based on crew size. Larger clans, with bigger ships and more votes, form the cores of political blocs. Opposition comes from the Outriders' Coalition, with delegates from thousands of smaller ships. The Admiralty defers to the Conclave's decisions in most circumstances. However, if all five members agree a Conclave decision jeopardized the survival of the fleet, and cannot get the Conclave to address their concerns, they have the right to summarily overturn the legislative decision. After the Admiralty uses this extraordinary power, they must resign. If the Admiralty does not step down after using their veto the rest of the military is obliged to arrest them. Each ship captain has authority over the vessel, but is advised by an elected civilian Council, just as the Admiralty is advised by the Conclave. This relationship may range from cooperation to polite tolerance to outright hostility, but any captain who overrules his council without good reason is relieved of command by the Admiralty. Many quarian ships are owned by clans who pool their resources to purchase used vessels from private sellers. Large ships are prestigious for big, rich clans, but a small ship means status for a small clan with enough personal wealth to afford a private vessel. Clan vessel captains are not subject to dismissal by the Admiralty; abusive captains are a "family" problem if they do not disrupt the operations of the fleet.
