Tali'Zorah vas Normandy came as a mandatory squadmate.

Tali's Trial Aboard the Rayya. 2185, some time after Tali rejoined Shepard the liveship Rayya at the Migrant Fleet — the garden plaza, then the hearing chamber The Admiralty Board reveals mid-hearing that the lab ship Alarei has been overrun by geth and that Tali's father, working aboard, is presumed dead. Tali refuses to accept it. Shepard and Tali propose to retake the Alarei; the hearing recesses pending what they find.

Tali's Trial Aboard the Rayya. 2185, some time after Tali rejoined Shepard the liveship Rayya at the Migrant Fleet — the garden plaza, then the hearing chamber Among the Admiralty Board members is Han'Gerrel vas Neema, commander of the Heavy Fleet and a friend of Tali's father from their days on the gunship Yaska. Han'Gerrel sympathizes with Tali, believing her innocent. He becomes the sole person Shepard and Tali can confide in about the true nature of Rael'Zorah's experiments on the Alarei; despite his pro-war stance, the revelation shocks him, and he vows to keep the truth quiet to protect Rael's legacy and what he intended for the Fleet.

Admiral Han'Gerrel vas Neema was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board and commander of the Heavy Fleet. He had a long history of provoking trouble along the turian border. A committed advocate of reclaiming the quarian homeworld, he argued that the Migrant Fleet had the largest fleet in the galaxy yet did nothing with it; Tali'Zorah countered that the ships might be needed against the Reapers, and he replied the quarians would need a homeworld to shelter non-combatants. Daro'Xen vas Moreh derisively called him "an aging warship," and he in turn dismissed Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib as a "whining suit-wetter."

Han'Gerrel was a friend of Tali's father, Rael'Zorah, having served with him aboard the gunship Yaska before their Pilgrimage. During a batarian raid that killed six of ten crew, the two, left alone on the bridge and under orders to hold position, disobeyed to recover a tramp freighter; they received medals and were sent on Pilgrimage early. During Tali's treason trial on the Migrant Fleet, Han'Gerrel sympathized with her and believed her innocent. He was the one person Shepard and Tali could confide in about the nature of Rael's experiments on the Alarei; despite his pro-war stance the experiments horrified him, and he vowed to keep the truth quiet to protect what Rael had wanted for the fleet.

Han'Gerrel was among the admirals who pushed for war against the geth, driving the synthetics to ally with the Reapers and trapping the Migrant Fleet within the Perseus Veil. When Shepard helped disable a geth dreadnought, Han'Gerrel ordered the fleet to press the attack on the geth flagship while Shepard's squad was still aboard. Back on the Normandy, Hackett and Shala'Raan condemned his recklessness, Raan threatening a treason charge. Shepard could hear his explanation or punch him and send him off the ship. He later clashed with Raan over comm about fleet maneuvering. After the Reaper controlling the geth was destroyed, Han'Gerrel ordered an all-out attack on the disabled geth fleet; whether he broke off depended on Shepard having earned the quarians' trust, and if not, the assault destroyed the entire Migrant Fleet.

Captain Ysin'Mal vas Idenna, usually called Captain Mal, was the quarian captain of the Idenna, a vessel of the Migrant Fleet. Unlike most conservative quarians, he was an aggressive proponent of change, notably advocating long-term missions for ships to leave the Flotilla and search for new homeworlds.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, Captain Mal welcomed Kahlee Sanders, Hendel Mitra and Gillian Grayson aboard the Idenna but privately warned Kahlee that the Migrant Fleet was less safe than it appeared. During a meeting with Admiralty Board and Conclave representatives he grew excited at mention of the Reapers, suggesting the quarians could find and reactivate one to control the geth and reclaim their homeworlds. He later confided to Kahlee and Hendel that the Flotilla was slowly dying, its ships breaking down faster than they could be replaced. Cerberus then attacked the Idenna; Captain Mal rallied and fought alongside his people but was being overwhelmed until Gillian Grayson intervened and Paul Grayson switched sides, warning them he had planted explosives to cripple the ship. Mal and Hendel disabled the explosives and saved the vessel.

Shaken, the Admiralty Board finally approved Mal's proposal, dispatching several cruisers including the Idenna on long-term missions to seek quarian survival through a Reaper or habitable planets. Mal hand-picked a crew of fifty, including Gillian, Hendel and the young quarian Lemm, judged Paul Grayson leniently by making him Kahlee's prisoner, and prepared to lead a five-year mission through a newly activated mass relay into uncharted space. In Mass Effect 2, Captain Ysin'Mal sent Commander Shepard a message of personal thanks for the Normandy SR-2's rescue of Lieutenant Forzan vas Idenna, the sole survivor of the crash of the Cyniad on Gei Hinnom.

This reference page cataloged every identified starship in the Mass Effect universe, giving each ship's class, affiliation, a brief description and its source work. Entries spanned Alliance, turian, asari, salarian, volus, geth, Collector, Reaper, Cerberus, batarian, Migrant Fleet, Andromeda Initiative and independent vessels, drawn from the games, novels, comics, Cerberus Daily News and DLC.

Notable Reaper entries included Sovereign, Harbinger, the Derelict Reaper above Mnemosyne, and the billion-year-old Leviathan of Dis. Council-race capital ships included the asari dreadnought Destiny Ascension (flagship of the Citadel Fleet, commanded by Matriarch Lidanya), the Geth Dreadnought destroyed by Commander Shepard in 2186, the Prothean flagship Penumbra Apex, and the Vol Protectorate's sole dreadnought Kwunu. The Alliance section listed the Everest- and Kilimanjaro-class dreadnoughts (SSV Everest, Kilimanjaro, Orizaba, Logan and others), numerous Fifth Fleet cruisers that fought at the Battle of the Citadel, and both Normandy frigates. Cerberus fielded the cruiser Elbrus under Oleg Petrovsky; the Blue Suns ran the prison ship Purgatory; Liara T'Soni inherited the Shadow Broker Base.

The Migrant Fleet accounted for many entries, including the liveships Rayya, Chayym and Shellen, Admiralty crew ships such as Neema, Tonbay, Moreh and Qwib-Qwib, and the lab ship Alarei. Dozens of independent MSV freighters (many Kowloon- or Athabasca-class) were logged, most lost to pirates, geth, mechanical failure or crew breakdown. The Andromeda Initiative section covered the arks Hyperion, Nexus, Natanus, Leusinia, Paarchero and Keelah Si'yah, the Pathfinder survey ship Tempest, and the ND1 Nomad; the kett fielded the Archon's flagship Verakan and the Decimation.

Admiral Rael'Zorah was Tali'Zorah's father and a member of the quarian Admiralty Board. As a young trainee alongside Han'Gerrel, he defended the gunship Yaska against a batarian attack, breaking formation in defiance of orders; the Admiralty Board awarded both trainees medals and sent them on their Pilgrimages early. Rael later rose to the Admiralty Board. He was distant and hard on Tali during her upbringing, determined that she become a capable representative of the quarian people, and driven by the goal of reclaiming Rannoch and building a house for his family there. In Mass Effect: Homeworlds and via vid-mail he impressed on Tali the importance of her Pilgrimage and the need for quarians to be strong. He approved her transfer to the Normandy SR-2 after Haestrom and sent Shepard a message about it.

In 2185 Rael had Tali send him deactivated geth components for a secret project aboard the ship Alarei. He was deliberately reactivating geth to experiment on hacking their neural network, violating sacred quarian laws that predated the flight from the homeworld. He refused his assistants' advice to alert the Admiralty Board, reasoning they would bicker and that he did not want Tali caught in political blowback. The reassembled geth turned on him and killed his entire research team. Tali was charged with treason and exile for sending active geth into the Migrant Fleet. She and Shepard boarded the Alarei, found Rael's corpse, and recovered a message on his omni-tool explaining how to deactivate the geth and instructing her to show the data to Han'Gerrel and Daro'Xen. Whether Shepard presented this evidence to the Admiralty Board affected Tali's trial. Told the truth in secret, Han'Gerrel vowed to keep it hidden. Tali stated that if Rael's deeds were exposed his name would be struck from every ship manifest and he would be remembered as the worst war criminal in quarian history.

In Mass Effect 3, if Tali survived and was not exiled, she temporarily filled Rael's Admiralty seat. Rael's experiments and Daro'Xen's subsequent breakthroughs directly caused the renewed quarian-geth war. After the events on Horizon, if she survived the reclamation of Rannoch, Tali reflected on her father over drinks at the Normandy bar, drawing parallels to Miranda Lawson's relationship with her own father; if romancing Shepard, she mused that Rael would have hated her human partner, and Shepard offered a toast to his memory.

**First Aid** is a tech talent available to Engineers, Sentinels, the Turian Agent, and the Asari Scientist, and is unlockable for Soldiers, Infiltrators, and the Quarian Machinist. Increasing ranks of First Aid increases the amount of health restored to the entire squad per use. First Aid differs from most tech talents in its use, activated through an independent hotkey (defaults are 'F' key for PC, 'Y' for 360, and 'Triangle' for PS3\). First Aid consumes 1 unit of medi\-gel per use. The amount of health restored per use is determined by the combined skill of the squad in First Aid. It can still be used even when there are **zero** points invested in the talent for any member of the squad including the player, but this restores only 40 points of health. Talent levels 6 and 12 are labeled as "Advanced First Aid" and "Master First Aid", respectively, but they provide no unique benefits other than a higher improvement to healing than other levels, barring the first. First Aid has a base cooldown period of 60 seconds (**Legendary Edition:**  20 seconds), which can be further reduced by some talents such as Medicine, many models of omni\-tool, and also the Asari Scientist class talent. Conversely, the cooldown can be increased if the player is affected by Damping. The First Aid achievement is unlocked by using First Aid 150 times. This also unlocks First Aid for use as a potential bonus talent for the Adept and Vanguard classes. Sentinels and Engineers trained as medics can use First Aid to revive downed squadmates and ignore toxic damage. This is the only method for reviving downed squadmates while in active combat on foot in Mass Effect other than the Unity ability that is unlocked from Spectre Training.

First Aid was a healing ability appearing as a tech talent in Mass Effect and as a power in Mass Effect 3. It was distinct from Unity, the squad revival ability of Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2.

In Mass Effect, First Aid was available to Engineers, Sentinels, the Turian Agent, and the Asari Scientist, and unlockable for Soldiers, Infiltrators, and the Quarian Machinist. It was activated through an independent hotkey and consumed one unit of medi-gel per use, restoring health to the entire squad based on the squad's combined skill in the talent. It could be used with zero points invested, restoring 40 health. Ranks 6 and 12 were labelled Advanced First Aid and Master First Aid but conferred no unique benefit beyond larger healing increments. The base cooldown was 60 seconds (reduced to 20 in Legendary Edition) and could be shortened by talents such as Medicine, many omni-tools, and the Asari Scientist class talent, or lengthened by Damping. Using First Aid 150 times unlocked an achievement and made the talent available as a bonus talent for Adepts and Vanguards. Sentinels and Engineers trained as medics could use it to revive downed squadmates in active combat and ignore toxic damage, otherwise possible only through Unity.

In Mass Effect 3, First Aid superseded Unity and was available to all single-player classes. Shepard could use it to heal NPC squadmates, revive fallen squadmates to full health and shields, and restore all of Shepard's health bars except on Insanity difficulty, where restoration was limited if Shepard was taking health damage. It affected only living squadmates' health, not shields, and squadmates could also be revived manually at no medi-gel cost, though First Aid was the only way to revive squadmates killed by instant-kill attacks such as a Banshee's impale. Each use expended no more than one unit of medi-gel, with a 50 percent chance of costing none if the Efficiency Increase upgrade was obtained. It had no recharge time and did not share the universal power cooldown, allowing near-constant use.

The Geth War, called the Morning War by the geth, was the conflict between the quarians and the geth that broke out after the geth developed sapience. The quarians created the geth sometime before 1895 CE as cheap labor and a military force, and to let them perform complex tasks unsupervised they allowed each geth process to share data across an advanced neural network. As more geth were built, this networking made them increasingly intelligent and they rapidly approached sapience. According to Legion, speaking to Commander Shepard and EDI in 2185 CE, in the quarian year 2485 a geth overseer named Hala'Dama was asked by a geth whether it had a soul and what its purpose was; she was not the first quarian asked, but the first to react with fear.

Recognizing the geth had evolved into a true AI, the quarian government ordered the immediate termination of all geth programs. A minority of quarians opposed this, arguing their society needed the geth and that questioning one's existence was no crime. When the now-sentient geth realized what was happening, they retaliated, initially only taking up arms to protect units that could not defend themselves. The quarians imposed martial law and hunted even non-hostile geth; dissenting quarians who sheltered geth were detained or killed. The opposition was overwhelmed and all-out war erupted in 1895 CE. The geth won within a year, overrunning the quarian colonies and the homeworld Rannoch and committing a genocide that killed all but a few million quarians, less than one percent of the pre-war population.

The survivors fled aboard their starships and formed the Migrant Fleet. Denied aid by the Citadel Council, they were stripped of their embassy as punishment for creating AI. The geth did not pursue the fleeing quarians, uncertain of the consequences of exterminating their own creators, and instead chose isolation behind the Perseus Veil, destroying emissary vessels that entered their space and killing organics who approached the Veil for the next three centuries. The Citadel stationed a fleet at the Veil's edge expecting an attack that never came, and later established a treaty with the quarians forbidding them from attacking the geth. Legion implied the geth felt remorse, tending abandoned quarian buildings like a cemetery and archiving and honoring the sacrifice of the quarians who had opposed the termination order, even though the quarians themselves had largely forgotten them.

Priority: Perseus Veil was a short, conversation-only mission acquired after Priority: The Citadel II. Following the failed Cerberus attack on the Citadel, Admiral Hackett told Shepard that the quarians were willing to aid the war effort with technical specialists and support ships, and directed the Normandy to the Far Rim. Shepard travelled to Dholen and docked with the Quarian Envoy Ship.

In the Normandy's war room the admirals of the Migrant Fleet explained that they had launched an open war against the geth, pushing them back toward the quarian homeworld Rannoch, after the Reapers gave the geth upgrades. The admirals asked the Normandy to help disable a geth dreadnought that was broadcasting the Reaper signal.

If Tali'Zorah had survived Mass Effect 2 she rejoined the squad; if she had not been exiled, she had been appointed an admiral in place of her late father Rael'Zorah. Even if exiled, Tali still appeared because of her knowledge of the geth, with the other admirals keeping her presence hidden, prompting Shepard to call her their "dirty little secret." Shepard could speak with Tali privately in the captain's cabin, continuing or locking in a romance, and on a first playthrough this unlocked Energy Drain as a bonus power.

In the aftermath, Admiral Shala'Raan vas Tonbay took up residence in the war room, Tali'Zorah vas Normandy became a temporary squad member, and the mission Priority: Geth Dreadnought became available.

Medicine was an unlockable tech talent in Mass Effect, available to Engineers and Sentinels but not the Quarian Machinist class. It lowered the cooldown of First Aid (by 10% at rank 2 up to 30% at rank 11) and unlocked the Neural Shock ability at ranks 1, 7 and 12 (Neural Shock, Advanced Neural Shock, Master Neural Shock).

Neural Shock induced paralysis and dealt toxic damage, working only on organic foes including humanoids, Husks, Thorian Creepers, rachni and varren. It had a fixed 45-second recharge and 60% accuracy cost at all ranks, doing 40/80/120 toxic damage and knocking out enemies for 1/3/5 seconds. It could drop any organic enemy instantly, making it useful against charging krogan, and its toxic damage suppressed enemy health regeneration. It had no area of effect and no proximity mine, requiring precise aim. Some enemies also possessed Neural Shock and could use it to disable Shepard or squadmates without landing a projectile.

The tour included his own sleeping quarters and the ship's trading deck, offering them insight into quarian culture and life aboard the Migrant Fleet.

Gardner in the Galley. 2185, aboard the Normandy SR-2 during the Collector mission the mess hall and galley on the crew deck of the Normandy SR-2 Mess Sergeant Rupert Gardner, the SR-2's cook and all-around handyman, tells Shepard he is "damn proud" of Cerberus — the Alliance and Council have their heads buried too deep to see straight. He was a family man working the frontier element-zero rigs until batarian raiders cost him everything, then joined Cerberus to make a difference. He calls himself a jack-of-all-trades who handles whatever "falls through the cracks," janitorial work and plumbing included, and concedes he cannot fight.

Gardner in the Galley. 2185, aboard the Normandy SR-2 during the Collector mission the mess hall and galley on the crew deck of the Normandy SR-2 Gardner's fate turns on the Omega 4 Relay timing: delay after the Collectors abduct the crew and he is processed into raw material with the rest; use the relay immediately and he is saved alongside Kelly Chambers and Dr. Chakwas. If he died at the Collector base, his name is added to the Normandy's Memorial Wall.

Gardner in the Galley. 2185, aboard the Normandy SR-2 during the Collector mission the mess hall and galley on the crew deck of the Normandy SR-2 If Shepard brings back the provisions, the crew notice the better food — Ken and Gabby down in Engineering, and Kasumi if she is aboard — and Gardner offers Shepard a sample of his calamari gumbo, revealing it is based on an asari recipe and joking that it seems mildly cannibalistic for a tentacled race to eat squid, though the asari "know good grub."

The galley functions as the ship's kitchen and dining facility. An L\-shaped seater with a table opposite the cooking area plus a couple of swivel chairs forms the room's structural arrangement. The galley supplies start out as meager rations from what little the Nexus has to spare. As the team progresses through the cluster, it eventually becomes stocked with fresh produce from newly\-founded outposts as well as newly\-discovered trading partners. Nakmor Drack claims the galley as his quarters upon joining the crew, though he can be found more often on other parts of the ship.

Once Javik has been integrated into the team, Vega reflects on his mental state, saying that it can mess with anybody's mind after being brought forward 50,000 years and being the last of one's kind. Vega hopes that despite all that, Javik will help with the war effort. He also laughs imagining the Illusive Man's reaction at his failure to secure the Prothean. evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-1 (Part 1) — Purpose and Interior
evidence.text: Reached by stairwells on either side of the CIC, Deck 2 holds the crew's living areas: the mess hall, crew sleeper pods, the captain's private cabin and office, escape-pod access, and the medical bay. Behind the med bay is a small science lab that doubles as auxiliary storage. The medical room has a medi-gel dispenser and several beds; lockers here are likely for senior personnel — Commander Shepard's personal locker is on this deck. The habitation deck looks compact for the stated crew size. Aside from the sleeper pods (used for stasis during crew rotations and non-relay flights) and the captain's double bed, there are no obvious full-time bunks, and no clearly visible galley, expanded storage, bathrooms, or exercise areas — implying either additional infrastructure outside the visible layout or crew-support functions distributed in ways not shown.
The complex environment of a starship interior made it essential to draw upon 3\-D sketching software to visualize such locations as the galley and sleep pod areas.
Various quality cuisine items used to prepare diplomatic dinners aboard starships. Rupert Gardner puts in a request to improve the mess hall experience aboard the Normandy SR\-2.

#### Mass Effect |  | Audio: Normandy SR\-1 | | --- | --- | The Normandy is a prototype starship, developed by the human Systems Alliance with the assistance of the Citadel Council. It is optimized for scouting and reconnaissance missions in unstable regions, using state\-of\-the\-art stealth technology. For most ships, the heat generated through standard operations is easily detectable against the absolute\-zero background of space. The Normandy, however, is able to temporarily sink this heat within the hull. Combined with refrigeration of the exterior hull, the ship can travel undetected for hours, or drift passively for days of covert observation. This is not without risk. The stored heat must eventually be radiated, or it will build to levels capable of cooking the crew alive. Another component of the stealth system is the Normandy’s revolutionary Tantalus drive, a mass effect core twice the standard size. The Tantalus drive generates mass concentrations that the Normandy 'falls into', allowing it to move without the use of heat\-emitting thrusters. #### Mass Effect 2 |  | Audio: Normandy SR\-1 | | --- | --- | The Systems Alliance Space Vehicle Normandy is a prototype starship created as a joint human and turian venture. A frigate optimized for reconnaissance missions, the vessel uses state\-of\-the\-art stealth technology. Most ships generate tremendous heat that is easily detectable against the absolute\-zero background of space. The Normandy, however, temporarily sinks this heat within its hull. Because of exterior hull refrigeration, the ship can travel undetected for hours, or drift passively for days of covert observation. That heat\-sinking carries the risk of cooking the crew alive if the stored heat is not eventually radiated. Also contributing to stealth is the Normandy's revolutionary Tantalus drive, a mass effect core double the standard size. The Tantalus generates mass concentrations that the Normandy "falls into," allowing it to move without the use of heat\-emitting thrusters.

Normandy: Special Ingredients was a short Mass Effect 2 assignment. After the mission Freedom's Progress, Shepard could speak to Mess Sergeant Gardner on the crew deck of the Normandy SR-2 and ask whether he needed anything. Gardner explained he wanted better ingredients to improve the crew's meals before the suicide mission, and that most of the supplies were available at the Citadel. Shepard traveled to Level 27 of the Citadel, visited the Zakera Cafe store, and purchased the High-Grade Provision for 500 credits, then returned it to Gardner to complete the assignment. The reward was 40 experience. Completing it caused crew members such as Crewman Goldstein to later remark on the improved food quality.

The SSV Normandy SR-1 (Systems Alliance Space Vehicle Normandy Stealth Reconnaissance-1) was a prototype "deep scout" frigate, first of the Normandy class, co-developed by the Systems Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy with Citadel Council sponsorship. Commissioned in 2183 and named for the 1944 Battle of Normandy, she was optimized for solo reconnaissance deep in unstable regions. She was initially commanded by Alliance officer Elli Zander, who was removed after clashing with turian chief engineer Octavio Tatum over the drive core's limits; David Anderson then took command, and shortly after handed the ship to Commander Shepard when Shepard became the first human Spectre.

The Normandy was built on three decks: a Command Deck with bridge, airlock, CIC and comm room; a habitation deck with quarters, mess, medical bay and captain's cabin; and an engineering and storage level holding the M35 Mako and the drive core. Her defining feature was the IES (internal emission sink) stealth system, which stored waste heat in lithium heat sinks, allowing silent running for hours; the system did not work at FTL and could be defeated by visual scan. It was powered by the experimental Tantalus Drive Core, roughly twice the size of a normal core and costing about 120 billion credits. Like all frigates she carried GARDIAN lasers, kinetic barriers, a spinal mass accelerator, and could mount Javelin disruptor torpedoes. Key crew included Joker (helmsman), Navigator Charles Pressly, Dr. Karin Chakwas, Engineer Greg Adams, Kaidan Alenko, Ashley Williams, and later Tali'Zorah nar Rayya, Garrus Vakarian and Urdnot Wrex.

During her shakedown the Normandy went to Eden Prime to recover a Prothean Beacon, which was destroyed during a geth attack. Rear Admiral Mikhailovich later inspected and criticized her as over-designed. When the Council refused to pursue Saren Arterius, Udina locked the ship down; with Anderson's help Shepard stole her and flew to Ilos. At the Battle of the Citadel the Normandy led the assault that destroyed Sovereign. In 2183 an unidentified starship (later revealed as a Collector cruiser) ambushed and destroyed the Normandy near Alchera, killing over twenty crew including Pressly; Shepard died saving Joker. Cerberus later built the larger Normandy SR-2 from the SR-1's design.

The Normandy SR-2 was the starship serving as Commander Shepard's base of operations after the SSV Normandy SR-1 was destroyed. It entered service in 2185, built by Cerberus at great and secret expense in the Voyager Cluster on the orders of the Illusive Man for the revived Shepard's team to stop the Collector abductions of human colonists; it served as headquarters of the Lazarus Cell. Based closely on the SR-1's layout, it was almost twice the mass of the original, added civilian-grade comforts (leather chairs, a kitchen), retained the SR-1's stealth characteristics, but could not land on every planet, requiring shore parties to use a Kodiak shuttle.

The ship had five decks: Deck 1, the Captain's Cabin ("the loft"), with a fish tank, model ship case, space hamster, and souvenir displays; Deck 2, the Combat Information Center, with bridge, galaxy map, armory, research/tech labs, and a communications room with a quantum entanglement array for real-time holographic contact with the Illusive Man; Deck 3, the crew's quarters, with the XO's office, mess hall run by Mess Sergeant Gardner, medical bay run by Dr. Karin Chakwas, the AI core, life support, main battery, and observation lounges; Deck 4, engineering, housing the oversized Tantalus drive core (three times the SR-1's, vertically oriented); and Deck 5, the hangar for the Kodiak shuttle and M-44 Hammerhead.

EDI (Enhanced Defense Intelligence) was the ship's AI, functioning as electronic-warfare defense with behavioral blocks preventing direct interface with ship systems, and serving as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears. She was designed in part from Sovereign's remains, making her partly Reaper-based. Armament included Javelin disruptor torpedoes and an upgradeable Turian-designed Thanix cannon (a miniature of Sovereign's weapon); defenses included kinetic barriers, cyclonic barrier technology multicore shielding, Silaris ablative armor, and GARDIAN lasers. Weapon, armor, and shield upgrades, plus the Reaper IFF recovered from the Derelict Reaper at Mnemosyne, determined crew survival in the final mission; the IFF also let the Collectors locate and board the ship.

By 2186 Shepard had defected from Cerberus and turned the ship over to the Systems Alliance, which refitted it, stripped Cerberus equipment, and recommissioned it as the SSV Normandy SR-2 in Alliance colors. Intended as Admiral Anderson's command center, it instead rescued Shepard from the Reaper invasion of Earth and became the mobile base for the war effort and the Crucible mission. In the final battle for Earth the Normandy deployed Shepard's team, then was caught in the Crucible's energy wave mid-jump and crash-landed on an unknown world; the severity of the crash and crew survival depended on galactic readiness.

Corporal Richard L. Jenkins was an Alliance Marine serving under Captain Anderson aboard the SSV Normandy. He was born in a rural district of Eden Prime and had dreamed of visiting more urban areas before enlisting, saying "even paradise gets boring." He wanted to prove himself as a notable soldier and test himself in combat, envied Commander Shepard's record, and admired the Spectres, being especially impressed by Nihlus Kryik after hearing that Nihlus once defeated an entire platoon single-handed, though his views were shaped more by vids than experience.

In Mass Effect, Jenkins was assigned to Shepard's ground team for the mission to Eden Prime and was killed by geth drones shortly after landing. His death was a blow to the morale of the Normandy's crew, who remembered him for his bold exuberance. Two years later, in Mass Effect 2, Doctor Chakwas recalled him during a drinking session with Shepard, telling how Jenkins was thrown back by a biotic display from Kaidan and, after Chakwas feared he had broken his back, jumped up shouting "That was awesome!" Chakwas cited Jenkins as one of the reasons she considered the Alliance great compared to Cerberus.

In 2186, the Normandy SR-2 received a memorial wall bearing the names of fallen crew from both the SR-2 and the SR-1, and Jenkins' name was included. If Shepard revisited Eden Prime, the Commander and some squadmates might briefly recall him and how he died on his birth world. Cut content from Mass Effect included a mess-hall scene, closely mirroring Chakwas' later story, in which Jenkins insists on Kaidan demonstrating his biotics and is tossed a cup before leaving disheartened for the cargo bay.

codex.text: - The Migrant Fleet was nominally under martial law but functioned democratically: each ship had an elected civilian council, ship representatives sat on the Conclave, and the five-member Admiralty Board could override the Conclave only by resigning or facing arrest afterward, done only four times in three centuries. (source: Migrant Fleet)

- Starships/List catalogs every identified vessel in the setting by class, affiliation and source, spanning Reaper capital ships (Sovereign, Harbinger, the Derelict Reaper, Leviathan of Dis), Council-race dreadnoughts, Alliance Everest- and Kilimanjaro-class dreadnoughts and Fifth Fleet cruisers, Migrant Fleet liveships and Admiralty ships, independent MSV freighters, and the Andromeda Initiative arks and the Pathfinder ship Tempest (source: Starships/List)

- The Migrant Fleet was organized into four groups: the Patrol Fleet (light frigates and fighters, internal security), the Civilian Fleet (majority of ships plus the three Liveships), the Heavy Fleet (main combat force), and Special Projects research vessels, each under a different Admiralty Board member. (source: Migrant Fleet)

- In Mass Effect 3 the quarians destroyed the geth megastructure at Rannoch, and the weakened geth accepted Reaper control code to survive; for the three endings — Legion's death, the quarian fleet burning, or peace bought by Legion's self-sacrifice — read `scenes/rannoch-the-choice-above-the-fleet.yaml` rather than a bullet: the causality does not survive compression. (source: Geth)
